A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SkillNav research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching relocated analyses and prompt listings.

before.justification: v1 reports original navigation experiments, skill evaluations, routing ablations, and temporal reasoning results, including Appendix Table 5.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds computational efficiency measurements and a human evaluation of routing.

M1.justification: The five DUET-based skill agents, two-stage training, temporal reordering, and two-phase top-1 routing procedure remain unchanged. Equations 1–6 and the wording of all five appendix prompts match; expanded explanations do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Training retains R2R, ScaleVLN augmentation, and the six synthetic skill datasets. Evaluation retains R2R, GSA-R2R, NavNuances, and the temporal subsets. The added timing and human routing checks reuse existing navigation coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds SAME to the R2R performance comparison; v1 cited SAME but did not include its results. The other navigation comparators remain, and SAME has no reported GSA-R2R entries.

E3.justification: The new efficiency study measures wall-clock runtime and throughput on A6000 hardware, using 14,400 and 9,000 predictions and a Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct implementation of MapGPT. v2 also introduces a 20-case human routing assessment. Existing navigation splits, metrics, and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds training and inference cost analyses, including the overhead of random skill selection, and a small human check of routing correctness. Existing skill, temporal reordering, router, and qualitative analyses remain; the Stop and Pause discussion is relocated to the appendix.

E5.justification: v2 newly reports a claimed high-confidence lower bound of 84% routing accuracy following 20 correct human-evaluated cases. It specifies neither the confidence level nor the calculation method. Both versions retain training seed 0 without additional repeated-run uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Added results cover SAME, computational costs, and 20/20 correct routing judgments. For example, v2 Table 5 reports Test-N-Basic throughput of 0.49 inferences/s for SkillNav versus 26.26 for ScaleVLN. Retained navigation scores in Tables 2–4 and v1 Table 5/v2 Table 6 are unchanged.

T1.justification: The graph, action, and routing formulations in Equations 1–6 retain the same mathematical content. Neither version adds formal proofs or theoretical guarantees; the new confidence statement supplies no mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: v2 replaces the abstract and introduction's R2R state-of-the-art claim with competitive or strong performance, while retaining the GSA-R2R leadership claim. It also foregrounds synthetic data generation as a contribution and adds an efficiency trade-off claim to the conclusion.

C2.justification: v2 newly discusses computational overhead, attributes the random variant's slowdown to lost batching, and frames training costs as an upfront investment. Its appendix explicitly identifies simulator-only evaluation and possible synthetic instruction biases as limitations. The existing stopping interpretation is retained.

D1.justification: v2 documents training times and the efficiency study's hardware, prediction counts, and MapGPT implementation. The printed code-access pointer changes from a repository to a project website. Existing training hyperparameters, trajectory-generation heuristics, and prompt wording remain available.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion and citations for Discuss Before Moving and FlexVLN and removes the deepfake-detection citation. It replaces v1's assertion that skill-based MoE methods have not been explored in VLN with an explicit comparison to the already-cited SAME, distinguishing SkillNav's explicit skills and independent grounding.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites affect the abstract, introduction, related work, method motivation, and conclusion. Headings are simplified, the appendix overview is removed, and the stopping discussion moves to the appendix. Most technical prose and prompt text remain intact, although several new section references render blank.

P2.justification: v2 adds the efficiency table and SAME row, expands Table 3's caption, and places table captions above their tables. The skill-distribution figure moves to the appendix, and the path-length chart shrinks from full width to one column. Existing figure content is retained.

improvement.justification: v2 improves claim calibration by withdrawing R2R state-of-the-art language despite unchanged results showing SRDF ahead, and by acknowledging SAME as prior VLN MoE work. The efficiency analysis and explicit limitations make practical trade-offs clearer. These are useful, limited gains; the small human routing check remains poorly documented, and blank section references introduce presentation defects.
